body: Quick pass: merges cleanly with main; body complete; author's quick gate green on 50c0bea7 at the first try (1259 tests), clippy clean on app and post; goldens byte-identical. Flagged ready; it decides what may be posted on a lathe's work spindle, so it gets the high-tier review. Sibling: PR #1191 (chuck rpm limit) decides the same "which spindle" question for its rule and will be rebuilt on this one's `lathe_voice` and `post/dialect.rs` - merge this first.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 50c0bea765f49e0d9907b9ef2f919f3cfba8d212 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers. I tried to break the lathe door several ways and every attack I tried held.

`git diff origin/main...head --stat -- crates/app/tests/golden crates/post/tests/recorded tests/golden assets/posts` is empty. The `PARAM LiveTool` condition in `post::dump` is the same expression moved into `dialect::states_live_tool` (`any(|m| m.rotary.is_some())`), so no section changes class. The stream is byte-identical.

### Probes (throwaway local tests, deleted, not pushed)
1. **A milling path with one C word** (the F1 face pass from the PR's bench, with `rotary = Some(0)` on its first rapid only). `voice` = `LiveTool`, so the door lets it through. The lathe post then voices the whole section on the live tool (`G98 / M1001 / M1003 S12000`, with no work-spindle `M03`) and refuses the moves: `post blocked - 2 warning(s): C move whose tip does not turn onto the live-tool station (C and X Y disagree) - refused, never projected; a move without a C word in a C-axis section - the spindle angle is unstated`. Tormach lathe: `... does not declare liveTooling ...; posed move (A/B/C words) on a 2-axis lathe`. So it is refused, and the work never turns at the cutter's rpm. `liveMove` refuses every C-less move in a live section, so a single C word cannot carry meridian feed moves through.
2. **A Drill 0.01 mm off centre**: refused. `D9: a Drill operation would be posted on the work spindle with a hole off the spindle axis (X0.010 Y0.000 from the work offset) - ...; keep the on-centre holes in an operation of their own and move it to a setup that posts through a mill post, or suppress the operation`. At 0.0004 mm (inside `SPINDLE_TOL` = 0.0005) it posts `G97 S10000 M03 / G00 X0 Z20 / G83 Z10 Q12000 F0.008`.
3. **Five holes, one at the centre and four at (+/-5, +/-5)**: the whole op is refused and the first off-axis hole is named (`X5.000 Y5.000`).
4. **A rigid tap on centre** (TAP-M4, `CycleChoice::Tap`) posts `G97 S800 M03 / G00 X0 Z20 / G84 Z10 F0.7`. The gate-free stream is identical, and `assets/posts` is untouched, so this is main's behaviour unchanged, not something the PR newly allows. A floating tap is still refused by the script (`floatingTapping is not declared`). Tormach lathe refuses tapping outright (no G33.1).
5. **The manifest reader**: `capabilities` is read by loading (evaluating) the script and then evaluating `typeof capabilities === "number" ? capabilities : null`. It is not a text scan. Results: a comment reads false, a string reads false, a conditional assignment reads whatever the branch set, and two assignments take the last one. `1e300` and `Infinity` read false, `6` / `3` / `2.5` read true, a throwing getter or a throwing script is `Err`, and `at_post` turns that into `post engine: ...`, a refusal and never a pass. There is no unwrap/expect/panic in `dialect.rs` or `lathe_voice.rs` outside tests.

### My own per-kind check
I enumerated `OpType` in `operation/types/sel.rs` against `want()` in `lathe_voice_tests.rs`: 41 kinds, which is 12 turning + Drill + 28 refused. Every variant is listed, and `want` is a `match` with no wildcard, so a new kind (e.g. `WireContour`) fails to compile until someone classifies it. The production `voice` uses `_ =>` for the refusal, so a new non-turning kind defaults to *refused*, which is the safe direction. No turning-family kind drives a rotating tool. Probe and PlasmaProfile get their own wording.

### Entry points
`post_script` (and therefore `post_setup`, single-mount `post_mounts*`, the script verb `cam.post`, and the MCP `post`, which goes through `post_mounts*`), multi-mount `post_each`, and `post_per_op*` all call `at_post` before the verifier and before any file is written. The GUI's Post and Post per operation call `post_mounts` / `post_per_op`. The only paths with no door are `stream_records` (no script) and the developer CLI `crates/post/src/bin/post.rs`. The CLI takes a hand-made stream and has no document or operation kinds, so it *will* post a milling `.cl` through a lathe script. Its own header says the in-app gate is what refuses, and I think that is acceptable for a developer tool.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Scripts with no `capabilities` line (#1199).** I would not make the stricter rule ("an undeclared script on a lathe or mill-turn machine is held to the door") part of this PR. On a pure lathe the family door (#530) already refuses every mill-family op, so the gap is only a mill-turn with a user's own lathe script that has dropped its manifest line. On a mill-turn, an undeclared script is just as likely to be a *mill* post, so the stricter rule would falsely refuse it. #1199 is the right place to decide that, e.g. by making a declared mask mandatory for custom posts.
- `lathe_voice::on_work_spindle` has no caller in this PR. Its doc says the workholding rpm limit reads it, which is presumably #1174's to wire. Meanwhile an on-centre Drill posts on the work spindle at the drill's rpm (10000 in the bench), as on main. Whether the chuck limit (#1031) judges that section is #1174's question.
- A pre-existing issue, outside this PR: `fanuc-lathe.cps` writes a "rigid" (`Auto`/`Tap`) tap as a bare `G84` with no rigid-mode word (`M29 S...` on Fanuc-style controls). Without it, many controls run G84 as a floating-holder cycle. Worth a follow-up issue if no one has filed it.
- `speaks_turning` loads the script once per op in `post_per_op`, which costs a little performance for nothing. Caching it per distinct script would do. Not blocking.
- Files: `lathe_voice.rs` is 176 lines with a provenance comment, and `posting.rs` grew by 3 lines. Tests sit in the owning crates. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1190`, and the subject follows conventional commits.

### What only a real control can prove
That a Fanuc-style lathe accepts the on-centre `G83`/`G84` with the work turning as posted (tap pitch vs `F` per rev, rigid mode), and that the live-tool words on a real mill-turn engage before C is commanded.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
